analysis:
Examined both workflow revisions, documentation patches, changelog and file metadata against the canonical definition index and supplied TB-002/TB-011 details. No independently supported vulnerability in this source scope. Provider authorization, attestation, encryption, cache isolation, billing ledger and privileged-helper controls are not changed here; no direct regression to their indexed threats is demonstrated.
.github/workflows/threat-model-review.yml head:68-85 restricts paid review to pull_request_target and retains default-branch scanner checkout without persisted credentials; PR source is not executed by the visible workflow. Head:64 retains explicit fork opt-in for Bedrock. Head:55,131,135-137 expands execution to 60 minutes, sets a 3000-second scanner deadline and replaces the 12-call/4096-token configuration with workload mode and defaults of 500 calls/16384 tokens. This increases potential paid resource exposure, but an exploitable budget bypass is not established without the adapter and admission implementation. Credential permissions, pinned actions, artifact paths and conditional clearance invocation remain unchanged.
Integration must verify .github/scripts/threat-model-review.py and its client/adapters enforce workload admission, emergency ceilings, bounded configuration, deadline-aware calls and reporting time, preserved OpenRouter spending limits, and rejection of paid reruns. Verify .github/scripts/threat-review-gate.py denies incomplete/stale results after timeout or cancellation. These are material unverified contracts, not observed missing controls. Changelog lines 3-13, docs/developer/build.md head:258-263 and docs/developer/test.md added lines 729-739 describe these protections but do not prove them; the workflow itself removes paid dispatch, not GitHub rerun capability. The next pass should reconcile those claims with implementation and tests.
